title: Outbound flight
context: Coasting toward the Moon; lunar module checks and mission communications.
timeBasis: UTC calendar day; mission times are from the uncorrected transcript.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. The scan on the camera makes the - that's a little bit better now. The flashlight seems to flicker, due to the scan on the TV. We can't see the eagle. Now it's a little bit better. Over. Could you open the f-stop a little bit more? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It's open all the way. We're going to have to move Buzz around a little bit.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. The color is better now. It's coming in. We could attempt a little bit better focus on it. There we go; it focuses a lot better now. We see the eagle coming right in on the lunar surface. Over. That's very good now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. That's very good now. We can see the Earth in the background, Apollo 11, and the eagle coming in.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It's probably pretty hard to see the olive branch, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. It is.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Well, that's what he has in his talons, is an olive branch.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're really impressed with the clarity and the detail that we have in the picture. The colors are - now, it's really an excellent picture now that I'm looking at it on our monitor, which is about 12 seconds before the networks can get it out due to the conversion that we have here on our TV converter. We're looking at the controls in the main display console. We can see the DSKY up on the panel. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That would be nice if you could take a look at all the circuit breakers; make sure the right ones are in and the right ones are out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Big Bubba's watching.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: And we're glad of it.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Boy, you guys have sure been doing a good job of watching us, Charlie. We appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: The spacecraft's been beautiful, 11. We've really no complaints at all. Looks - Things are really great.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Can you see this DSKY on the MDC?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. It appears that - can't quite tell what program ... went P00. We see you punching in a VERB 35, I think it is. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. Might as well tell the EECOMM's - or tell the GNC and everybody to hold on to their hat and I'll push the EKTER button.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We see a real display now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's a good demonstration of how the crew has the interface with the computer, talking to the programs and all that we have in the computer.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Well, that's right, Charlie. Sometimes it tells us things and sometimes we tell it things and mostly it talks to us.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston, We just lost our pic - I see we're going back outside now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. We copy, and as we pan back out to the distance at which we see the Earth, well, it's Apollo 11 signing off.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Apollo 11. Thank you much for the show. It's a real good half hour. Appreciate it. Thank you very much. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. That's it, Cnarlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We appreciate the show. Thank you very much. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Would you key ERROR RESET on the DSKY, please? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. We should be straightened out now, Charlie, and back in P00.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. How do we stand on this O2 fuel cell purge? You want to go ahead and do that as scheduled in the flight plan?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by, 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. You can commence the O2 fuel cell purge now if you'd like. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: While Buzz is doing that, I'll change the lithium hydroxide.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. The attitude that we're in right now is a convenient one to start PTC in. We'd be satisfied with this attitude. So we'd like you to disable quads Charlie and Delta; and we'll wait about 5 to 10 minutes, and than we'll establish the PTC. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Disable Charlie and Delta, and we'll wait before starting PTC.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11, Houston. The rates are damped out well enough for you to initiate the PTC now. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get it going.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. This time the DAP didn't like 0.3. It's - We followed the procedures; we got down to 70 000 ENTER. It took off at about 0.7.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're copying that. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Would you like high gain back?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And you - Would you select ATTITUDE HOLD? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston. Would you say again what your request is?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. We'd like you to go back to ATTITUDE HOLD. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Looks like we're going to have to reinitialate - reinitialize this PTC.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any roll angle that you'd like to stop it in, Charlie? I haven't stopped it yet.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. It's your preference. Right now if you want to. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. The problem on that initially - starting up the PTC was we failed to do the VERB 49 which - and load the desired initial attitude; so the DAP tried to take it back to the old attitude that we had started up in number of hours to go. That's why we picked up the rates in the other axes. We're going to wait in this attitude for about 20 minutes to dump out the rates again, and than we'll proceed with the VERB 49 and load our attitude that we have at the time - at this time. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. That sounds good, Charlie. When you get to the VERB 49, I'd like for you to give me the three gimbal angles that you want loaded.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'll do. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And Apollo 11, Houston. We have your flyby PAD if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by one.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Is that P30 PAD?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: All right, Buzz. It's - flyby is the purpose. SPS/G&N: 62815, plus 097, minus 020 070 54 5944, minus 00028, plus 00023, plus 00069 029 149 312, apogee is NA, plus 00221 00078 001 00034, sextant star 01 2385 227, boresight star is NA NA NA. Latitude is minus 0265, minus 16500, 11899 36228, 144 56 47. In the comments: your set stars are Deneb and Vega, 007 144 068. No ullage. It's a docked burn using the PTC REFSMMAT. Stand by for your readback. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Would you give me GET of O.05g again, please?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. 144 56 47. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Flyby SPS/G&N: 62815, plus 097, minus 020 070 54 5944, minus 00028, plus 00023, plus 00069, 269 149 312 NA, plus 00221 00078 001 00034, 01 2185 227 NA, minus 0265, minus 16500 11899 36228 144 56 47, Deneb and Vega, 007 144 068. No ullage; docked, PTC REFSMMAT. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Say again your roll angle, Buzz. I copy - I read 029. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. 029.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Good readback.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. On the 0.7 rate, the rate loaded into the DAP is 0.1 or 0.2.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Go.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. Would you please copy down your VERB 16 NOUN 20 ICDU angles now, then execute a VERB 49 and load that - those angles, the NOUN 20 that you see on the DSKY into the VERB - into the NOUN 22 slot; and PRO on that, and that will start our 20-minute rate period. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Charlie. I'll do that right now in just a matter of inches. Those numbers are plus 04511, plus 09021, and plus 35984. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. I've done that and, of course, I got an immediate 50 18. So I guess we're set up to proceed from here, and I'll start the 20-minute timer.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston. I still question that 0.7 rate with 0.2 loaded into the DAP, though. Could you explain that one?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're working on it.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We got a little laser visual experiment we'd like to - for you to do for us. If - if you got the Earth through any of your windows or through the telescope, would you so advise? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by one, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: At this roll attitude, what should our highgain angles be? Maybe that would help us locate you. We don't see you in the lens.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Those high gain angles are pitch minus 70, yaw 90. We think the Earth is apparently pretty close to plus z-axis. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Charlie. I got you in the telescope.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Apollo 11. We've got a laser that we're going to - It's a blue-green laser that we're going to flash on and off at a frequency of on for a second, off for a second. It's coming out of McDonald Observatory near El Paso, which is - should be right on the terminator - or right inside the terminator. We are going to activate that momentarily. Would you please take a look through the telescope and see if you can see it. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Telescope? Or sextant?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Either one. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, I'll try it with the telescope; and if I don't see it there, then I'll try the sextant.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'll give you the word when they've got it turned on. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. They don't have it turned on yet. We'll give you the word when they got it turned on. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We noticed the CRYO pressure dropped a moment ago. Did you stir up the CRYO's? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. We've finished our cycling operations.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. McDonald's got the laser turned on, Would you take a look? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: It's bluish-green.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We got some shaft and trunnion for you that might tweak it up a little bit. Shaft of 141.5, trunnion of 39.5. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. If you see it, it should be coming up - appear to be coming up, through the clouds. McDonald reports that there's a break in the clouds that they're beaming this thing through. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. You can terminate the exercise on the Laser. Our rates are steady enough now for - to commence the PTC. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okays Houston. Neither Neil nor Mike can see it. Incidentally, those shafts and trunnions just missed pointing at the world.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: As we are looking at it through the scanning telescope, it would be about a - oh, maybe a third of an Earth radii high and to the left.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: But, we did - but we did identify the El Paso area and it appeared to us to be a break in the clouds there, and we looked in that break and saw nothing.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you much. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Go ahead. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Were you following that on the DSKY?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. What's your exact question? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I've followed the procedure through step 7 down to the point where I've got 27303 ENTER, and this resulted in an OPERATOR ERROR LIGHT.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Stand by a moment. We'll have an answer for you momentarily. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Appreciate it, Charlie. Now the light's gone out without any further DSKY action.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Correction. Stand by; that's not so.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We've finally gotten concurrence on our problem here with 50 guys looking at it. When we were sitting in the 5018, we attempted to load the erasable before you terminated the VERB 49. So Mike, what we're going to have to do is call up the present CDU's, copy those down, and do a VERB 49, load the present, then do a PROCEED, then an ENTER, and then we can then set up ATTITUDE HOLD in step 6. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. I think that's what we did last time.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: It appeared to us that we attempted to load the erasable prior to entering on the VERB 49 which VERB 49 was still running, and it clobbered the CDU's. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. We're moving at the proper rate.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hallelujah!

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. It looks great to us now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It looks fine here, Charlie. The 0.7 part is the only part I don't find explained yet.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. We're working on that one right now. We're coming up with the story soon. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We're handing over C0MM to Goldstone. Over. Correction, from Goldstone to Honeysuckle. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Hello, Houston through Honeysuckle. Ov - -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Go ahead. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You sound good to us through Honeysuckle. How do we sound?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You're five-by, Mike. We'd like the OMNI configuration as follows. OMNI Alfa place in Bravo, OMNI to OMNI, high-gain track to MANUAL, high-gain yaw 270, pitch - -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. How do you read now? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I'm reading you loud and clear. I'm not sure I got all those. I've got S-band OMNI B, 0MNI, track to MANUAL, and beam wide, pitch - you'd better say that again, and yaw 270. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. I broke up at pitch minus 50 at beam wide. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Are you ready to copy some numbers on status report, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Are you ready to copy some numbers on the status report, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Go ahead. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Radiation CDR 11005, CMP l0006, LMP 09007; medication negative. And I got some battery and RCS numbers for you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Battery C 37.1, PYRO battery A and B both 37.1. RCS Alfa 82, Bravo 84, Cocoa 85, Delta 87. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, we copy. Radiation 11005, 10006, 09007; no medication; 37.1, 37.1, 37.1, 82, 84, 85, 87. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: That's affirmative. And you want a LM/CM DELTA-V? It's 1.1.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy 1.1.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Please verify that four CRYO heaters AUTO, the four fans off. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. We have been holding the O2 heater number 1 in the OFF position. I believe that was your last instruction. All the other heaters are AUTO and all fans are off. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We would like all heaters AUTO. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. All four AUTO, all four fans off.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. As the Sun sinks slowly in the west, the White Team bids you good night. If we get a story on the seven-tenths, we can give it to you in about 15 minutes or so; if not, we'll give it to you in the morning. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. That sounds fine, Charlie. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Hey, you earned your pay today, Charlie. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Good night all.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. One request: the optics switch to zero. And we've got a lot of theories on why it maneuvered at seven-tenths a moment ago, Mike, but no real definite answer. We'll be back with you later. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. No rush, Charlie. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Mike, I think we can explain that seventenths rate. When we - the first time through, you know, we failed to go through the VERB 49, so we had a large error between our actual CDU and desired CDU in roll. And with that situation, the DAP - the vehicle will roll - will maneuver, rather, at a rate that is loaded in, which was three-tenths plus four-tenths rate, and it will limit at four-tenths above the desired rate, so - that is if we have a large enough angle between the desired and the actual, which we did. So, therefore, the rate was four tenths plus three tenths to give you the seven tenths. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Houston. Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Good morning, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: ... nice sleep. Be getting around to the ...

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: How's everything look up here from the ground?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Roger. Say again, please.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. How do all our systems look?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. They're looking great, and as far as we can tell everything is good from down here. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Looks like the attitude held up real well during PTC last night.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes, it did. We were showing you remaining well within a circle of 10 degrees radius throughout the night. Seems to be working beautifully.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: How's the old Green Team this morning? Did you have a quiet night?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a very quiet night. Down here the old Black Team is complaining they didn't get a chance to make any transmissions. Ron Evans is getting

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Well, we'll be seeing them tomorrow, I guess.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes. Ron's getting to be known as the silent CAP COMM.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's the best kind, Bruce.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: (Laughter) Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: When you feel up to copying, 11, I've got a couple of small items in the way of a flight plan update and your morning consumables update. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. We'd like to perform a waste-water dump at your convenience some time in the near future here. No particular time scheduled. Down air at the time for midcourse correction 3, which is about 53 55, we're deleting midcourse correction number 3 and all the items associated with it. For your information, the calculated value of the burn for midcourse number 3 was eight tenths of a foot per second, that is 0.8 feet per second. Canceling this, if we decide to burn midcourse correction 4, this would then give you a burn for midcourse correction 4 of 2.0 feet per second. At 53 hours we have an IMU realign P52. We're requesting that you do this while in PTC, and we plan to continue PTC throughout the day. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: - then we'll get to the waste-water dump - -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again, please. You're cutting out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. - -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. Stand by a minute, please. We're having difficulty receiving you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Radio check. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger, Houston. Read you loud and clear. How me? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Reading you the same. We did a minor reconfiguration down here. Stand by. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay, 11. This is Houston. We switched your OMNI antennas as you rolled through the appropriate position. Did you copy the flight plan update item?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Apollo 11, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. Did you copy the flight plan update items? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. How do you read me now, Bruce?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. The battery charge is in the process now and the wastewater dump is in work. MCC 3 has been canceled. It would have been 0.8 feet per second. MCC 4 now looks like about 2.4 feet per second. At around 53 hours we'll do a P52 in PTC. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. The magnitudes of the midcourse corrections were just for your information, but midcourse 4 was down around 2.0 feet per second. Again, for your information, on SPS chamber pressure, it looks like your onboard readout of 87 psi corresponds to 92 psi by our telemetry, and your value of 89 on board corresponds to 94. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Radio check on a new power amplifier in our transmitter. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear. How me? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Loud and clear. Did you copy my notes on SPS chamber pressure?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Negative.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Just for your information again, it appears that your readout of 87 psi corresponds to our corrected TM readout of 92 - that's 92 psi, and 89 on board is really 94 psi. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger, I got that you were reading about 5 psi low.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And are you ready for the consumables update?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Consumables update for GET of 46 plus 00: minus 5.5 percent, minus 6.5 percent, minus 2.5 percent, minus 7.5 percent, minus 5.0 percent, minus 2 pounds hydrogen, plus 1 pound oxygen, and that minus 5.5 percent on the RCS total corresponds to minus 66 pounds. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. I copy those, and I'll give you our percentages now: Alpha 82, Bravo 84, Cocoa 85, Delta 87. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: This is Houston. We copy your percentages, and do you have a crew status report on sleep For us?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. And in descending oeder 8, 9, and 8. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Houston. Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, we're getting CRYO pressure warning now in the middle of stirring up the ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. We've got the continent of Africa ... facing toward us right now, and of course, everything's getting smaller and smaller as time goes on. The Mediterranean is completely clear. The Sun looks like it's about to set around Madagascar. The equatorial belt of Africa stands out quite clearly. We're seeing the dark green or a muddy colored green, compared to the sandier colors in the southern tip of Africa and, of course, the Sahara northern coast of Africa. There's a rather remarkable cloud that appears in the vicinity of the border between Afghanistan and Pakistan. It's just about to go into the sunset now. It is casting quite a large shadow. It's isolated. There don't seem to be any other clouds ... the band of clouds near the tropical conversions clouds down around the equator clearly separate the clockwise and the counterclockwise cloud formations. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. We copy your word description on that. I understand you can see a shadow being cast by that cloud over between Afghanistan and Pakistan. Any estimate on how long that shadow would be? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: It looks like it's a shadow. Coming around to - back that way - -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We're getting a lot of background noise now, also. If you will stand by a minute or so until we roll a little further in PTC, I think things will get better.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. It's coming around to the number 1 window. We'll get you ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, we're hearing you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. The noise on the COMM seems to have quieted down now. I guess that we've rotated a new antenna into view and probably also the Earth out of view in your window. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. It looks as though the length of the shadow of that cloud is about the same as the width of the Persian Gulf.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. We copy the width of the Persian Gulf, and I guess that all I can give you firsthand is a single isolated data point, and that is that it was clear here in Houston this morning. That's a pretty localized observation. As a result of your waste water dump, it looks like the PTC mode has been disturbed somewhat. We're showing you about 20 degrees out in pitch right now and about 6 degrees in yaw, which is significantly greater, about twice as much - a little more than twice as much as the deviation you had prior to the waste water dump. We' re watching it down here, though, and we'll let you know if we think any corrective action is required. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe we ought to - next time split that in half, and put half of it on one side and half on the other or something like that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes. We could do that. We were actually pretty interested in seeing what the effect on PTC would be of the waste water dump. We don't recall ever having performed a waste water dump during PTC on previous missions. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, now we know.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. I am looking at that cloud now around Pakistan through the sextant, and it appears to be one single cell in the latter stages of development. There is a smaller, more isolated one - -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. We lost you down in the noise on the COMM link here about the time you were describing the single cell cloud formation over Afghanistan-Pakistan area through the sextant. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. It came through a lot clearer through the sextant than with the monocular, and you could definitely tell it was one single cell in the latter stages of development. It must have gone up to over 50,000 feet, though. The eastern Mediterranean is phenomenally clear. You can see all the lakes; the Dead Sea stood out quite well. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. What appears to be the limit of resolution through that sextant from your current position? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, I can't see it right now. It's outside the field of view.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And, I don't know yow you'd really describe the limit of resolution. I will think about that a little.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. I guess the smallest object that you could pick out looking through it would give us a pretty good hack.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, you can see the Nile River going almost up to its source. The lake is obscured by clouds, but you can trace it all the way on up.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I guess that is down though, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We have been working under the assumption that it would take about an hour for the interference from a waste water dump to dissipate to the point where you could reasonably take star sightings for platform alignment navigation or something of this sort. If you have a spare minute or two, could you comment on the observation condition, now? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. Stand by one, Bruce.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: My guess would be the telescope's probably pretty useless, but you can differentiate in the sextant between water droplets and stars by the difference in their motions.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay, Mike. I guess that we've still got - what you are saying is that we've still got a lot of water droplets visible, but you can pick them out and distinguish them in the sextant, then.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Right. I think so. Buzz is looking through it now. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. It looks like at this time the sextant would be quite usable for any alignment. There's actually very few ... verticals.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. How about the telescope? Is it useful now?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, it's not quite as useful; it never seems to be. Depending on the position of the Sun, it's got that band that seems to go across the center. I don't think it's because of the waste water particles that it would lack its effectiveness. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. What - Is this band something that's deposited on the outside of the optics? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: No. I see the reflection from the Sun.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: The Sun bounces off the LM structure. With the LM attached, that telescope is just about useless. Those star charts that MPAD provided us, I think, would be most useful if we had to use the - if for some reason we had to mark through the telescope. We could use those as a guide for what we're looking at and say, "Well, that bright blob over there has got to be that star because that's the position we're in." But so far, we've not been able to pick out any decent star patterns while docked with the LM using the telescope.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: This is Houston. We copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Go ahead - -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: - - How do your read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're reading you loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. You're coming back a little scratchy. It,looks like our O2 flow transducer's gotten a good bit worse. I just looked at it at the last water accumulator cycling, and it just barely registered - barely crept up above 0.2. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. At the time of your cyclic accumulator stroking, we were on low-bit-rate data, and consequently not receiving the O2 flow parameter. We expect that what you're seeing is probably nominal. That is, it's probably what we would expect from a transducer that's malfunctioning probably in this fashion, and it's just going to keep on getting worse like that. Nothing to worry about. We'll monitor things on the ground here. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. It does look like it's gradually degrading to about zilch.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11 CDR, this is Houston. Radio check. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger, Houston. CDR. Loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're reading you the same. Out.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And would you check with FAO and see where that errata sheet is? We haven't been able to locate that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. I understand it's supposed to be the back page in Buzz's operational checklist.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Did you find it? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We found it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And I see you're in P00. If you can give us ACCEPT, we'll uplink a new state vector to you and update the CMC clock. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. You've got it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. We're through with the uplink. You can go back to BLOCK.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Back to BLOCK.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. We woudd like to terminate the charge on battery B at GET of 51 30. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. We would like to terminate charging battery Bravo at 51 30 GET. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Terminate charging battery Bravo 51 30.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. We show you terminating battery B charge. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston. Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. We show you terminating battery B charge at about 51 hours 30 minutes. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Would you like to have both oxygen and hydrogen purge on? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. Say again. Both what on? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: On the fuel cell purge: would you like to see both oxygen and hydrogen? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Affirmative. We request hydrogen and an oxygen fuel cell purge. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Any preference which first?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Negative. As long as you've got the H2 purge line heaters on.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. I'll go get - Go ahead with the hydrogen then.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. You copy my NOUN 93?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. We've got it.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. I am going to go ahead and thrust then. Triangle difference is 0.01, but it's sort of difficult at three-tenths rate. I'm required to use medium speed unresolved, and it's difficult to hold the star centered long enough to get a decent mark on it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy. It looks okay to us.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. I've got the morning news here if you're interested. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes, we sure are. We're ready to copy and comment. Isn't that 2:30 there?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Go.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Here we go. The interest in the Flight of Apollo 11 continues at a high level but a competing interest in the Houston area is the easing of watering rules. Mayor Louie Welch promises a lifting of lawn-watering restrictions if the rains continue. Friday is partly cloudy, and there is a 30-percent chance of thunderstorms in the afternoon. In Washington, D.C., the Senate Finance Committee approved extension of the income tax surtax, but a Senate vote on the bill - -

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You cut out, Houston. You cut out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Where do you hold me cutting out? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. How do you read now? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Loud and clear, Houston. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Start after the rains in Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. In Washington, the Senate Finance Committee has approved extension of the income tax surtax, but a Senate vote on the bill currently seemed remote. In Austin, State Representative Ray Lemmon of Houston has been nominated as the National Director of the American Society for Oceanography. Lemmon has proposed a study of the possibility of establishing an institute of oceanography in Texas. This would be the first such institute on the western Gulf of Mexico. In Minneapolis, Minnesota, the weather bureau, after recapping today's weather showing a high of 88 and a low of 72, has noted "snowfall: none." From St. Petersburg, Florida, comes a radio report from the Norwegian explorer, Thor Heyerdahl, which said that the crew of his papyrus boat, the Ra, will sail into Bridgetown, Barbados, despite damage from heavy seas. The crew, however, will sleep on an escort vessel. Norman Baker, navigator of the expedition, said the crew was aboard the Ra today repairing damage from storms this past week, which split the footing of the mast. Part of the broken mast was jettisoned overboard, and the vessel was 725 miles east of the Barbados. "It is possible but uncomfortable to sleep aboard the Ra," Baker said in the radio report. "But the purpose of our voyage is not a test of strength or human endurance." That is the reason why the crew was spending nights aboard the escort vessel Shenandoah, which rendezvoused with the Ra on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: In sports, the Houston Oilers are showing plenty of enthusiasm in their early preseason workouts at Kerrville, and Coach Wally Lemm says he is impressed with the fine group of rookies. National League baseball yesterday, Thursday: St. Louis 11, Philadelphia 3; Montreal 5, over Pittsburg 4; Atlanta 12, Cincinnati 2; San Fransciso 14, and Los Angeles 13. American League: we have Baltimore 3, over Cleveland 2; Detroit 4 to Washington's 3; Minnesota 8 to Chicago 5. Boston at New York was rained out. And in Corby, England, an Irishman, John Coyle has won the world's porridge eating championship by consuming 23 bowls of instant oatmeal in a 10-minute time limit from a field of 35 other competitors. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. I assume Houston didn't play yesterday.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I'd like to enter Aldrin in the oatmeal eating contest next time.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Is he pretty good at that?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: He's doing his share up here.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Let's see. You all just finished a meal not long ago, too, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I'm still eating.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Does that - that - -

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: He's on his - He's on his 19th bowl.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Are you having any difficulties with gas in the food bags like the 10 crew reported?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Well, that's intermittently affirmative, Bruce. We have these two hydrogen filters, which work fine as long as you don't hook them up to a food bag. But the entry way into the food bag has enough back pressure to cause the - the filters to start losing their efficiency. A couple of times, I've been tempted to go through that dryout procedure, but we found that simply by leaving the filters alone for a couple of hours, their efficiency seems to be restored.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Their efficiency ranges anywhere from darn near perfect to terrible just depending on the individual characteristics of the food bags we're putting through them. Some of the food bags are so crimped near the entry-way that there's no way we can work them loose to prevent back pressure.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Hello, Houston. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. As you've probably noticed, your coning angle in PTC mode is increased substantially as a result of the waste water dump, the fuel cell purge, and a natural coupling, so it looks like we are going to have to terminate PTC here in a little while. And we'd like to get your feeling as to whether you're still anticipating trying to send back TV signals from inside the LM; and if so, we'll try to provide an attitude that you can hold that'll give us high gain antenna lock on the Earth during the TV and LM activation period. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Yes, we're still planning that activity if the cord lengths work out all right, and we'll accept those attitudes that you work up for us.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: This is Houston. Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: When you work up an attitude to get high gain, is there any way that we could get partial Sun in one of the two LM front windows?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: This is Houston. We'll have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We have a TV attitude for you if you're ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead. Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. We recommend stopping PTC at GET of 54 45 00, and this should put you at just about the right roll angle. The attitude we recommend is roll 263, pitch 090, yaw 000. This gives you the Earth out of window number 1 in the command module and places the high gain antenna in the CSM window for TV at your convenience. You will also have the Sun shining in - or shining at the hatch on the LM, and if you take down the window shades you should get some sunlight in. We're recommending wide deadband. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you, Houston. We'll look at that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. When we pass the proper roll angle, we're not going to be anywhere near zero degrees yaw. Do you want us to just stop and try until we find ourselves in and then VERB 49 the three angles you gave us?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We'd like you to stop at the proper roll angle, then do a VERB 49 to the roll and pitch. Over. Correction, roll and yaw.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. Do you read me? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by, Charlie. Yes, we'r going to come out of PTC here at 263 roll and then do VERB 49 to thc recommended attitude.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That sounds fine to us. Ovcr.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Before you open the pressure equalization valve, we'd like the LM/CM DELTA-P. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Let me check it again. It was about 155.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I read it 158 right now, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you much.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. We're stopping PTC at 263 ... 0.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. You're about one-by on this transmission. Say again. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Do you read?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. How do you read on the high gain?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, how do you read me? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Read you loud and clear, Charlie. We just switched to HIGH GAIN, and we stopped PTC at roll 263, pitch 90, yaw 0. How do you read?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. You're five-by now on the high gain. We're right between the 0MNI antennas and pretty horrible COMM on the OMNI's. We got you five-by on the high gain, and we copy the PTC stoppage. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, we're going to open the DIRECT O2 valve and start pumping up the cabin.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're going to hand over to Goldstone for uplink in about 2 minutes. We might have a momentary dropout of COMM. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Alright. Can you hear our master alarm in the background? That's O2 FLOW HIGH coming through this amplifier.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That photoelectric cell is a good device. It's worked very well.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Say again. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I say that photoelectric cell amplifier for the master alarm is a good device. It's working very well, and it's a nice pleasing tone.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Makes you almost glad to get master alarms.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. As a matter of curiosity, our O2 flow meter is pegged FULL-SCALE HIGH.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. We copy that here. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Boy, that transducer's working somewhat.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We'd like to try to attempt to correlate your O2 flow in transducer with the flow valve that you've got open. How far - How far open would you say you have the REPRESS O2? 0ver. Correction, the DIRECT O2.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Charlie. It's not open very far. It's hard to give you a good reading without shunting it again, but the arrow is at about the one o'clock position. Now I reduce the flow, and I'll let it stabilize here. Right now our onboard reading is about 0.4, and that's with the arrow in the O2 valve at the two o'clock position. Would you rather have comparisons of O2 flow readings or would you rather have valve position comparisons?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: EECOMM's say they'd like to look at valve positions. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we're holding steady now at 0.3 pound per hour, and our cabin pressure is about 54; and I'll close the valve momentarily and then open it again to this position and tell you how much travel is required.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It's about 30 degrees of travel, Charlie, from the closed position, which is with the arrow pointing at about three to three-thirty, four o'clock.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Our flow is stabilized now at 0.6.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy. We're reading the same.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes, open it back to the one o'clock position.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: And thanks for putting me on relay, Houston. I was missing all the action.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Is that enough different positions, or you want more, Charlie?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Mike, that's good - good enough. We're satisfied now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. We've terminated direct O2, our cabin pressure is 57, and, as a matter of curiosity, when we turn the DIRECT O2 valve OFF, we get a master alarm just like they did in the spacecraft testing.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston, we have a little update for you. When you go into the LM, we'd like you to unstow and bring back to the command module the following items. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'd like you to pick up the - out of the flight data file, the surface checklist, the mission rules NO-GO card, the DPS, APS, RCS limit cue card. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. The reason we wanted you to bring those three items back, we'll have some updates for you, for those three. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. We figured you would.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're getting the TV at Goldstone. We're not quite configured here at Houston for the transmission. We'll be up in a couple of minutes. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. This is just for free. This isn't what we had in mind.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. It's a pretty good show here. It looks like you almost got the probe out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes, it's loose now.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil. It's really good.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Not much light up in that area, but apparently the TV set's able to pick it up.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: There are some bright spots shining on the probe. Apparently Sun shafting on it that just gets just about enough for us to make it out. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: I think those are the tunnel lights.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Oh, Okay. You're right.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. It's loose now. Coming down.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Looks like it's a little bit easier than doing that in the chamber.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: You bet. This is the only way ...

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You have to take it easy.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: It's pretty massive, but it goes where you direct it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That's a beautiful picture now, we've got. We're looking at a 12-second delay. To us you are just bringing it down by the optics now.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Mike must have done a smooth job in that docking. There isn't a dent or a mark on the probe.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We're really getting a great picture here, 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. With a 12-foot cable, we estimate you should have about 5 to 6 feet excess when you get the camera into the LM. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We can see the probe now. Correction, the drogue.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Drogue removal's coming next.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. As we suspected.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Now it's a good view of the storage area under the couch.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Looks like you're pretty crowded in there with that drogue. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Oh, it's not really bad.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: This TV cable is getting in the way.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We see lots of arms.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: The only problem, Charlie, is these TV stagehands don't know where they stand.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Well, you got to really have a union card, there. We can't really complain too much, I guess.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Do you have a little white dot in the bottom of your monitor - TV monitor? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We do.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. I guess part of the camera's been burnt out down there. These are really beautiful pictures now, Buzz. Over. Real clear.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. We might have got just a little bit of Sun in there. Is it just one small white dot?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: We went up in the tunnel checking the roll angle, Charlie, and it's 2.05 degrees.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy. 2.05 on the roll CAL.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: And that's a plus.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Plus.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. The tunnel looks pretty clear to us. Somebody going up there now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: It's Mike checking his connectors up there now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. The lighting up in there looks very good to us at this time. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: I think that's mostly the camera. It - it's subdued to say the least.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. It's pretty - It's gathering pretty well to us. We see everything quite clearly up in there.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Well, the docking latches look good today just like they did yesterday. Everything up in there looks just fine.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That sounds fine to us. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We can even read the decals up there on the LM hatch.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, let me zoom it up and see how much you can read.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We can see the LM umbilical connection quite well there, Buzz. We see you zooming in on one of the decals now. It's, "To reset, unlatch handle; latch behind grip and pull back two full strokes." That's about all we can make out.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Hey, you get an A-plus.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. At least I passed my eye test.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I'm standing 6 feet from it, Charlie, and you can read it better than I can. There's something wrong with the system.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's a real good view of the LM hatch handle there, 11. 0ver.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Looks like we'll be ready to go into the LM early if that's okay with you all down there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. It's fine with us, Neil. Go ahead anytime you wish. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. The white spot you see on your monitor, our TV people say it is a burn spot; but they expect it to dissipate after a couple of hours. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, the dump valve is actuated.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy, 11. We see that very clearly. Is that you, Buzz, with your hand on it?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We're really amazed at the quality of the picture up in the tunnel. It's really superb. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: It is, considering the amount of light up in there.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. We're about to open our hatch now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. There's that same guy that, when you open up the door, why, he's waiting there for you, and he turns the lights on.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: How about that. Just like the refrigerator.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Buzz, the view in through your - by your right - left shoulder there is so good we can see the ascent engine cover, the Velcro on it, and that's about all we can make out right now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Now we can see the helmet stowage bag - -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We don't see anything loose up there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Well, great. Looks good to us. We see the helmet storage bag.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, 11. Houston. We got a view of the PLSS there, off the right of our screen.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Buzz, you already in? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I'm halfway in, hanging out. Start turning around, I guess.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We'd like you to read out the LCG reservoir sight level. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, we have a good view of the window there. It looks like the Sun's finally coming through the shade.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes, I'm afraid it's - We're just about plus Z toward the Sun.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. This attitude put both windows right toward the Sun - or the LM. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, that may be good in some respects, but -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We had a view, Buzz, of the utility light cord. ...

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Now let me show you a view looking the other way.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And we see right now the utility light or either the floodlight up there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: I think now I see the utility light still in the stowage bag. Hey, that's a great shot right there. We see you in there. Guess that's Neil and Mike. Better be, anyway.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We see you waving.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That's really a beautiful shot.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We didn't quite decipher that signal that just came from the CMP.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Just saying hello. On the LCG sight gage, you got about - oh, it looks like the white mark that's in the plunger is about a quarter to three-eighths inch out into the green away from the red. Is that what you'd like to see? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by. Roger, Buzz. That looks good to us. Thank you much.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: It is the white index, is it not, that you're interested in comparing whether it's in the red or green?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by. That's affirmative, Buzz. It looks good. That's a good reading for us. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We had a shot moment - a moment ago of the suit disconnect valve.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I'll open up the windows and see what the lighting condition's going to be like.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That's a real good view we have of the AOT. You're back now, Buzz, and notice you're taking down one of the window shades. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: The light is superb.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: How's the Sun coming in? How's the Sun coming in from this direction going to affect what you can see?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: It made it really super. The lighting is excellent in the - in the LM right now. We can make out the AOT, the ISA, and the left-hand window - there's a little glare off of that, but the LMP side the - with the shade down it's really excellent. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, let's - I'm turned around, why I took the shade off my side first.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy. The light level for the TV is really excellent. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Yes, the lighting in the LM is very nice now, just like completely daylight; and everything is visible. A good bit lighter than the tunnel was earlier.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We got a good view now, Neil, of the DEDA; and also Buzz's ACA.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Hey, I'm pointing it at the front hatch now. Everything seems to be in place down there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, we got the dump valves in view. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We see you removing the ISA now, folding it up, putting it up on the AOT. The instrument panels are coming into view behind.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes, I think it'd probably be best, since we've done SPS burn, to put it back over the instrument panel instead of putting it up over the PLSS on the recharge station. Would you care to comment on that one? We could do either just as easily.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by. We'll have an answer for you momentarily.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That's really a super shot of the main display.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: The vehicle is surprisingly free of any debris floating around. It's very clean.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. It's pretty hard to describe this view. It's really - really great.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Now you know how we feel.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Neil's OPS is about 57, 5800.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And mine's about 5800, also.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That's a good shot of Neil's PLSS, there. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: No, that's mine.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That moment - a moment ago, we had a good shot of your PLSS, Buzz, and the two helmet stowage bags. Down behind your left shoulder, Buzz, we have the - the DSKY and the ACA.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We're going to go ahead and take all the Moon data on back into the command module, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Buzz, it appears that you're intending to put on the Sun filter and view the Sun through the AOT. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately it looks like it's down a little bit more towards ... than I can be able to see in the AOT.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We got a beautiful view of the side of the command module out of the AOT looking in the left rear detent.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I can see the hatch and all the - all the EVA handrails. First time we've seen the silvery outside of the command module.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I can read the letters on the hatch cover. It's a boost cover release; and the big yellow arrow that points toward the opening - place where the tool B goes.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Great shot now back down into the -

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: And left on the - -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, Buzz. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Say again.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: I was just saying we got a great shot looking back into the command module.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. And the left detent, I can see the AO - or the rendezvous radar, and I move to the forward detent and that's about all I've got. I'm looking eyeball to eyeball.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Charlie, is there any concern about the duration that we ought to have the window shades open?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We don't have - We don't have any circulation in here, and it might get a little on the warm side.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: We'll - We'll put up a couple of hoses in the command module here and get a little circulation going.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Sounds like a good idea. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. As far as the window shades go in this LM, there's nothing except for crew comfort. I don't think we've got any systems problem. Be sure to put them back up when you egress. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: That we will do.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Charlie, I'll give you a view out of the overhead window, back looking at the command module right-hand rendezvous window.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Well, we see it now. Thanks a lot, Buzz. That's a good view through the overhead.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: One washer on -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: One washer's on by the overhead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: There we go. We got it now.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: There wasn't very much debris in the command module or the LM. We found very few loose particles of bolts, nuts, and screws and lint and things. Very few in each spacecraft. They were very clean.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Sounds good.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We have a good view out of the rendezvous - correction, the overhead window of the LM. We don't see anybody staring back at us, though. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Charlie, can you see Mike's two eyeballs staring out through the rendezvous window?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Stand by. We haven't picked him up yet.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: You are looking through a lot of layers of glass.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We had a - -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: ... on my monitor.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We had a slight glimpse of Mike in the rendezvous window at that time. It's pretty murky looking into there, though.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Here he is; I've got him. I've got, him on the monitor now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. We see him staring back at us now. Hello, in there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Our recommendation for the ISA is to stow it back over the instrument panel. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Will do.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We can make out the markings on the panel. We read SYSTEM A ASCENT FUEL, ASCENT OXIDIZER. Quad 1, quad 4. The - It's really unbelievable, the definition we're getting down here off that little camera. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We can even see the barber pole on the talkbacks.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We can read the markings on the instruments for the glycol pressure, quantity, PCO2. You can even read the scale on the eight ball. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We see the cross-feed barber pole, and we have the Velcro patches back up to the RCS systems now. We can see the markings on the meters, green and red bands, in limits.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We see you raised the cover on the abort stage. We don't recommend that.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes. We're going to tape that one over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We're going to tape that one over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We concur.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: The restraints in here do a pretty good job of pulling my pants down.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We haven't quite got that before the 50,000,000 TV audience, yet.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That's a good view of the eight ball. We see - You can even read the OFF flag, there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: You can see the signal strength meter for the radar, read the numbers on it.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, did you want us to test the cameras in the LM and - I was wondering about that. I saw it in the flight plan, but I'm just wondering if you want to do that on CSM power, or do you want us to take both of the 16mm cameras back in the CSM and test them there? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by, Buzz.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: As an alternative to that, why, we could wait LOI day and do it then when we transfer over to LM power.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by. We'll have an answer.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. On that TV, our commentary - The monitor I was looking at was delayed about 12 seconds, 12 to 15 seconds while it went through our color converter. It was probably - You thought I was crazy, but we were looking at it 15 seconds after you broadcast it. 11, Houston - -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We understood that, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. On the LM cameras, we'd like you to do it on LOI day with the LM power. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. That's what we'll do.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, we're showing you something that came out of the Commander's checklist stowage packet. It's got a 16-millimeter camera in it, and it's got this little cylinder; and I guess - I don't understand what it is. Maybe you can tell us.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by. We can't figure it out either.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: It's got an arrow on the back, and it says "turn," but I'm afraid to turn it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, your friendly geologist says it's the camera cank- crank, excuse me, for the 16-sequence camera if it jams. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: All very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: There's that word again. The ancillary stowage container.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: The shades couldn't quite hack it, there, Buzz. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, 11. Are you still getting high bit rate off the OMNI's at this distance?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by, Mike.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. About 50 percent of the time, we're getting high bit rate off the OMNI's when you're in PTC. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Neil, at this attitude you look like you're about 12 feet long.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: It seems like I always find myself upside-down in whatever I'm doing around here.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Could you give us a few comments on your crew comfort with the CSM hoses moving the air around? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Well, it's picking up a little bit on circulation in here.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: What do you estimate the temperature is, Buzz? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Oh, I'd say maybe 73, 75.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: It's hard to tell at this density and pressure of gas, but comfort level is about the - about the same as the command module.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: You probably - -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: It was a little warmer or stuffier when we first got in, but it seems to be improving.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Houston copies. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston.

utterances.speaker: LMP
