utterances.text: You may be able to see some - -

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: - - some particles jumping around on your screen. That's just dust particles that are being illuminated by Sun shafting in the window.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. They're very clear now. Over. And that's a good view of Neil's - correction, of Buzz's circuit breaker panel, there.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I can just barely see the handrail on the front porch from the position on the right-hand window.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Our view of the Panel 11 is - gets brighter, then darker. Are you changing the f-stop at all? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: No, what's happening is, we get pretty close to the window now and then, and it drives the automatic light control into the stop, I think.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes, I had the switch on OUTSIDE while I was going through the overhead window. That may be what's contributing to some of it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We seem to be picking up a few more dust particles now. We see them quite clearly in the screen now. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes, I'm choking on one every so often.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Your show is going out to the U.S. now. We're about to get the satellite up. It'll be transmitted to some other countries after that. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I'm checking out this window bracket where I'll be putting it for the EVA pictures of Neil going down the ladder.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We keep marveling about the color and the clarity of the picture. It's really difficult to describe. It's - It's just perfect. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And, 11, it doesn't look like you're having too much trouble with that bracket up there, Buzz.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I'll tell you, those new knobs really make it easy to twist the thing and get it cinched down quite tight.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Buzz, how does the alignment look, there?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: It looks pretty good, as well as I can tell without the gear extended. I can't get a real definitive answer, but you couldn't fix it any place to see much more out of the window without hand-holding it for the whole time.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Looks like to us it's going to work real well.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Give it enough room to - Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Buzz, we see you putting your window guard in place there, and back up to the ISA now.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, ask FAO if the 90-degree bracket isn't stowed in the Commander's stowage assembly.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Buzz, you still looking for that 90-degree bracket? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Yes, he is looking for it now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'll have a word for you in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Our monitor shows pretty good, clear pictures from this angle. I already found the 90-degree bracket.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil. It's really a super picture. We've got the ACA, your ACA, the picture of the throttle, the 90-degree bracket. We see your handles, and now over to the bracket.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: That's about the position we'll be putting the camera in after the initial descent on the ladder, and it'll be taken 1 frame a second for most of the EVA.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Houston copies. Out. That's a real good view of that camera.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Our monitor is a little bit wavy, so it's hard for us to tell when we're - when we've got a steady picture for you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, we have no complaints at all. We don't see that waviness on our picture. It's just really great. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Do the edges of the window look like straight lines to you?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. They don't in our monitor, and that leads us to make some corrections to the camera, which probably aren't required sometimes.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Buzz, we have no complaints at all. It's a magnificent picture.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: What was that, Buzz, you're chasing now?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: That was - That was me picking up some particles of paint that were floating through the air in front of the camera, there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil. We got it. It appears to us that Neil's about to check the Velcro mat, there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay, Buzz. We see the card up now.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. For those of you that don't know, this is where we log most of our data for each of the LM maneuvers, and we have another card like this that the timeline book that is laid down on the table in front of the data display keyboard; and it's on this timeline that we have all our procedures. But we obviously have to hold these in place in zero g, so we make use of the Velcro patches on the back and on the table so we can attach these down here; and then we just turn the pages over when we go to new sequences in our timeline of procedures.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And we're ready to copy DOI PAD.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'll have the FIDO's work that one up for you momentarily.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That was a good shot of Panel 2. Now we got Panel 3 in view with the TEMP MONITOR switch. The stabilization - station and control panel, we see now, with the MODE CONTROL switches. Now over to the rendezvous radar. Real good.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, that's real good camera work.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: That'll be the most unusual position a cameraman's ever had, hanging by his toes from a tunnel and taking the picture upside-down.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Well you're doing a super job. We got a good view of the cross pointer, there. Had a good view of the tape meter.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We're giving you a picture now of the floor of the cabin. I think you can see the - one of the two portable life support system backpacks here in the center, and on each side, we have the two helmet visors. I'll remove one of them and show you a little closer view of what this looks like.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Inside the helmet visors are the EVA gloves with the blue tips. I'm about to take those out now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. That's a great shot now that we're getting of the helmet, the EVA visor, and also the - the EVA gloves in the background.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. You did say this was going out now, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Standby. I think so.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, you got a pretty big audience. It's live in the U.S. It's going live to Japan, western Europe, and much of South America. Everybody reports very good color. Appreciate the great show.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Buzz, that was a good demonstration of your EVA visor assembly. Appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hey, I like the good view of Mr. Collins down there. We finally see him again.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Hello there, earthling.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We noticed when you were scanning over Panel 2 a moment ago, 1 and 2, the two eight balls were slightly in disagreement. Control said he'd like a AGS align, there.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes. One of them's AGS, one of them's PNGCS. The problem is, we don't know whether to align AGS to PNGCS or PNGCS to AGS.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Chris said he can tell you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: We'll cage them both.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Like old home week, Charlie, to get back in the LM again.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. I can imagine.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: The traverse from the bottom of the LM to the aft bulkhead of the command module must be about 16, 20 feet. It's not a disorienting one at all, but it's most interesting to contemplate just pushing off from one and bounding on into the other vehicle all the way through the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Must be some experience. Is Collins going to go in and look around?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: We're willing to let him go but he hasn't come up with the price of the ticket yet.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. I'd advise him to keep his hands off the switches.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: If I can get him to keep his hands off my DSKY, it'd be a fair swap.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's why I've been eating so much today. I haven't had anything to do. He won't let me touch it any more.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. If that's not the Earth, we're in trouble.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: That's the Earth, and we have a very good view of it today. There are a few more cloud bands on than yesterday when we beamed down to you, but it's a beautiful sight.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: We have some horizontal banding in our TV monitor. Are we transmitting that to you, or do you have a clear picture?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Neil, we have a very clear picture. The only thing that we see is a little white dot in the bottom of our screen, which is - our TV guys say is an - apparently a burned out spot in the camera, but it should come back. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. We have that in our monitor also.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We do have three lines across our TV. I thought it was just a transmission problem, but everybody's telling me now that it's probably - it's on the downlink. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: No, those are the same three ones that we have.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: How far are - out are we now, Charlie?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by. Give you exact figure.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Did you notice the difference between yesterday and today? This is as large an image we can - we can give you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. If you think we're smaller, you're now 177,000 miles out. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: That's nautical miles?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative, 11. We -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: ... Hold on.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We see the - still see the banding along the intratropical convergence. I guess the most predominate one now is around the - up in the - around the equator or slightly north of the equator.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way it looks, Charlie. Same as yesterday.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Just keep the Pacific Ocean nice and clear and calm on splash day, is all we ask.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And Charlie, I'd like to say hello to all my fellow scouts and scouters at Farragut State Park in Idaho having a National Jamboree there this week; and Apollo 11 would like to send them best wishes.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Thank you, Apollo 11. I'm sure that, if they didn't hear that, they'll get the word through the news, surely appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We have you - your subspacecraft point is just off the western coast of South America directly south of about Mexico City. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: That - That looks like what we observe from here.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And we're going to turn our TV monitor off now for a short bit while we have some other work to do. Apollo 11 signing off.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. Thank you very much. That was one of the greatest shows we've ever seen. We sure appreciate it. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: It was a pleasure.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Could you give us an idea of about how long it will be before you start close - closing the LM back up? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: We've got a little more work to do up here, Charlie. We're going to make sure that we have everything transferred around and stowed the way we want it and try to get a little bit ahead on tomorrow's timeline. I suppose that we could be out of there in another half hour or so if it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil. We're not trying to push you. We're just trying to get an idea of - about water dumps and starting up the PTC again. Take your sweet time. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. We'd like to get a flight plan update from you for the next couple of hours, here. When you think what the various constraints might be and what - what order you might like us to do things.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by. We'll have that to you in a moment.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Mike, we'd like to go ahead and do a waste-water dump. We'd like you to dump it all the way down to zero. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. We copy that, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: How does that work, Charlie?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Did you call? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Just noticed that the mast that the EVA light is on is charred brown. It looks as though it took quite a beating during launch.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: The EVA light still does work.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'll let this - the SPAN guys look at this, and we'll be back with you with what we think. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We were wondering, Neil, with your closing comment on the TV, if you were going to turn it off. It indicated that you might be considering turning it back on. We were wondering whether we want to keep the lines up. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Well, we want your recommendation on that, but I think we would just as soon, ourselves, terminate the TV. But if you have a commitment to keep, we'd be more than willing to turn it back on.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We'd like to terminate the TV. We don't - We think we got a really - a good tape. That hour and a half show was superb. And we'd like to pick up TV - correction - PTC at about 58 hours. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. PTC at 58 hours.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And we'll have the remaining functions in the flight plan soon. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Our recommendations on the activities for the next hour or so, as far as flight plan goes, are: Continue your LM familiarization as desired until about 58 hours, then ingress to the CSM, close the hatch, and establish PTC shortly thereafter. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And, Apollo 11, Houston. Terminate the - -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: - - the water dump. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay, Charlie. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Water dump being terminated now.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger, Houston. I'd like to do a P52 option 3 and tweak the platform up prior to starting the PTC. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. That sounds like a good idea to us. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. And the platform's looking pretty good to me. It looks like the worst axis drift is 0.01 something degrees per hour. Is that about what you figure?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Roger. We've had reports all the marks have been good all the - the last couple of times you've run them. Just a moment; I'll get you some information on the apparent drift rate.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Owen. Thank you. You got the maroons on?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again, 11.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I say you got the maroons on now?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Not permanently, Mike. Just have a stand-by here while Charlie's out checking how to use that special tool on the camera. The maroon team will be on tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Nice to hear your voice. How's everything going?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Everything's going smoothly here. We sure enjoyed the show this afternoon, Mike.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We suggest you go ahead and do the P52 first, and we'll take a look at the angles and give you some new drift rates after taking a look at them. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead. 11, here.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. A little information to you there, CDR. We've all taken a momentary brief respite from out work here to have some special - to have a bite of special moon cheese that is - I understand it's been sent to us directly from Wapakoneta, your own hometown. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: No, we can't - we can't pronounce it either. I think you'll enjoy that. They make a fine brand of cheese.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, there, and I'll polish up the grammar for the next trip.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, 11. You are looking at the NOUN 93, and I'll proceed when you copy them.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We've got them.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11, Houston. We'd like P00 and ACCEPT. We have a DELTA-H update for you. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: All right, Charlie. Stand by one.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. P00 and ACCEPT.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We got the load in. The computer's yours. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, 11. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We'd like for you to stir up the CRYO's now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. We're completed in the LM. We're closing up the hatches and the probe and drogue back in.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We're standing by to watch your startup on the PTC at any time. You can start off at the VERB 49. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Wilco. We're just finishing up the probe and about to close up the hatch here. We're going to be a couple of minutes late, probably, getting started in the PTC.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. No sweat, 11. We're standing by. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Mike, there's no wait required. Where rates are steady, you can proceed on. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I'm doing it, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: The tunnel's all taken care of, the drogue, probe, and hatch all back.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We have some new additions to your alternate contingency checklist if you would break that out. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay, Houston. 11's ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. If you'll turn to page F2-22. 0ver

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. I have F2-22.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil. Under column 1 - that's column Lima, line 06. The new data is 00001. Line 07, the new data is 02134. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. I have in F2-22, column Lima, item 6, 00001; item 7, 02134.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. That's correct. Thank you much. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. For your information, those two entries are an update to your DELTA-H that we have already uplinked into the CMC. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: What was I marking on, Charlie? About an 18-kilometer line, or what?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We - Our update puts you to - the DELTA-H to 35 kilometers, Mike. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We've got some switch positions for you for the high gain. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. Select Bravo, 0MNI, HIGH-GAIN TRACK to MANUAL; BEAM, WIDE. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Bravo, 0MNI; TRACK, MANUAL; and BEAM, WIDE.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And your high-gain angles are minus 50 on the pitch, 270 on the yaw. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Going there now.
